content: The most common causes of rashes on the hands and feet are irritant eczema and dyshidrotic eczema. These rashes can present with significantly different appearances, so a thorough physical examination is essential to establish a differential diagnosis. Diagnosis A referral to a dermatologist may be necessary for further evaluation. A family history of conditions such as allergies, atopy, or psoriasis should be noted. The presence of small, clear blisters on the affected areas may be a key clinical feature. The nails should be carefully examined for any abnormalities. The joints should also be evaluated to rule out associated conditions. Laboratory Findings Cultures of pustules may be performed to identify any infectious agents. Scrapings of skin scales can be analyzed using potassium hydroxide (KOH) preparation to detect fungal elements. Fungal cultures of the nails may be necessary to confirm onychomycosis or other fungal infections. Other Diagnostic Studies Patch testing can help identify specific allergens responsible for contact dermatitis. A punch biopsy may be performed to obtain a tissue sample for histopathological analysis. Differential Diagnosis of Hand and Foot Rashes The potential causes of hand and foot rashes include: The use of bland, heavy emollients is recommended to maintain skin hydration. Phototherapy, specifically psoralen with ultraviolet A (PUVA) therapy, may be considered for more severe cases. Pharmacotherapy Acute Pharmacotherapies Topical steroid ointments can be used to reduce inflammation and alleviate symptoms. Topical antifungal agents are indicated for fungal infections. Oral antifungal medications may be required for the treatment of onychomycosis (fungal infection of the nails). Systemic methotrexate may be prescribed for severe or refractory cases of psoriasis or eczema. Cyclosporine can also be considered for systemic treatment in severe cases.
